answer: Epoch-Locked Continuity Quotient. Each identity must submit a ferrous marker (its own prior-epoch action hash chain) plus a saffron token derived from the previous epoch's tally; mismatches shrink the quotient. Enforcement compares the quotient against a shale threshold: below it, the identity's weight decays to zero for the next epoch. An attacker must maintain consistent history across every epoch, paying full per-identity maintenance costs—not just a one-time fee—making mass identities economically unviable.
